convention: literal line-by-line, as in batch H09's brief
reasoning_summary:
3.6.13-15: paene goes with delevit and occupatam with urbem in the next line, so the fragments are kept and noted; hic/ille glossed as Aethiops/Dacus. 3.6.29-30: non sine conscio | marito is split across the lines, with the double negative kept.
3.7.8: insomnis may be nominative (Gyges) or accusative plural with noctis; the order is kept and the ambiguity noted. 3.7.32: duram (with te) and difficilis (nominative) are kept as two predicates.
3.8.13-16: cyathos amici sospitis centum is rendered with the genitive 'of your friend being safe', with a note on the toast-genitive; esto's subject is split over lines 15-16.
3.9: dialogue; each speaker (the man / Lydia) is marked in the note on the first line of the stanza, and the source's quotation marks are left out of the English (as noted). Line 12 has no final stop in the source.
3.10.3-4: incolis Aquilonibus is split (native | Aquilones), and the missing stop after line 4 is noted; 19-20 non hoc semper ... latus keeps the genitives with patiens.
3.11: the Cerberus stanza (17-20) is doubted by some editors and is translated as printed; inane lymphae dolium and in omne ... aevum are split across lines; quotation marks are kept for Hypermestra's speech (37-52) and noted.
3.12 (Ionics): the tibi datives of separation and the agitato grege / arto fruticeto ablatives are left split across lines.
